caseno: Appeal from Original Order No.5 of 1985 with Civil Rule No. 25(fm) of 1985
lawyer:
Mozammel Hossain with Kamal-ul-Alam, MA Hakim ----- For the Appellants. 
Maqbul Ahmed with MA Jalil ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
ASM Amanullah & others ----- Petitioner
vs
Chittagong Municipal Corporation ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Jalil J : This appeal at the instance of the plaintiffs is directed against the Judgment and order dated 17-1-1985 passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong in Title Suit No. 60 of 1983 rejecting an application for temporary injunction under Order 39, rules 1 & 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. The plaintiffs filed the aforesaid suit for declaration of title to the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint and for recovery of possession contending, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to Waqf Estate of Khan Bahadur Sheikh Hamidullah and Sheikh Abdullah Khan. After the death of its Mutwalli Sk. Abdul Aziz Khan one ABM Shayesta Khan became the Mutwalli of the said Waqf Estate in terms of Tauliatnama of 1889 and he had been in possession of the Waqf properties. During the 2nd World War the suit property was requisitioned by the Government for the purpose of using it as trenching ground of the Chittagong Municipality in and LA Case No. 11 /45-46 under the provisions of the Defence of India Rules framed under the Defence of India Act, 1939. After cessation of war the Defence of India Act and the Rules made thereunder expired and all requisitioned lands including the suit land stood released from requisition. 

 The suit land was not acquired by any notification at any time. The owner Mutwalli ABM Shayesta Khan entered into possession of the suit land some time in 1947 by fixing boundary pillars and by putting fencing in open denial of the title of the Chittagong Municipality. While thus in possession the said Mutwalli leased out the same to the plaintiffs for 99 years in 1951 and since then they have been in possession of the same and thereby they acquired good and indefeasible title to the suit land by lease and adverse possession continuously for nearly 36 years. In January 1982 the Chittagong Paurashava published a public notice inviting applications from intending lessees for leasing out the plots of lands within Muradpur Residential Area and on enquiry the plaintiffs came to know that the suit land was also included in the said notification. The plaintiffs served the Paurashava with a notice on 12-4-82 under section 152 of the Chittagong Paurashava Ordinance, 1977. The said Paurashava has been renamed as the Chittagong Municipal Corporation under the provisions of the Chittagong Municipal Corporation Ordinance, 1982, repealing the Chittagong Paurashava Ordinance, 1977 and the plaintiffs served another notice on 7-2-83 under section 161 of the said Ordinance on defendant No. 1 the Chittagong Municipal Corporation demanding exclusion of the suit land from the layout of the Muradpur Residential Area and stopping disturbance in the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs produced necessary papers for perusal of the Deputy Administrator of defendant No. 1. On 7-2-83 the employees and workers of the defendant No.1 removed the boundary pillars and fencing of the plaintiffs, fixed some pillars of their own encroaching upon the land of the plaintiff's and on 11-2-83 they started cutting and digging earth for road construction and thereby they forcibly dispossessed the plaintiffs from suit land and, as such, the plaintiffs have been compelled to file the suit. 

 3. The plaintiffs also filed an application under order XXXIX, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for temporary injunction restraining defendant No. 1 the Chittagong Municipal Corporation from cutting earth and digging ditches or trenches and from levelling the hill slopes and from making any constructions in the suit land and from transferring the suit land to anybody also till the disposal of the suit or from changing the nature and character of the suit land. It was alleged in the said application that the defendant No. 1 has taken a scheme to convert the suit lands which are tilla slopes and plain lands. into a residential land by cutting the hill slopes and by digging trenches and if the hill slopes are cut the lateral support of the adjacent eastern hill of the plaintiffs would slide down resulting in collapse of the plaintiff's pucca building standing thereon. 

 4. The defendant No. 1 contested the said application for temporary injunction by filing a written objection denying the material allegations and contending, in substance, that the application is beyond the scope of Order 39, rules I and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that the plaintiffs have no prima facie case for injunction and that the application is barred by the provisions of Martial Law Order No. 40 of 1932 and also under section 161 of the Chittagong Municipal Corporation Ordinance, 1982 for want of valid notice. It was further alleged in that written objection that the plaintiffs have no manner of right, title, interest or possession in the suit land or in any part thereof. 0.145 acre from the southern part of suit plot No., 16 along with other lands has duly acquired by the Collector, Chittagong under the provisions of LA Act I of 1893 in LA Case No. 11 of 1945-46 on 26-3-1942 and the remaining land of the suit plot was acquired in GL Case No. 2 of 1943-44 on 16-1-1944 by the Collector, Chittagong under the same Act and accordingly possession of the suit land was made over to the Chittagong Municipality in both the cases and since the said dates of acquisition the defendant No.1 has been in continuous possession of the suit land in respect of the suit plot one Abdul Wadud and 9 others claiming through the predecessor of the present plaintiffs, filed Other Suit No. 76 of 1965 against Chittagong Municipality for declaration of title to a portion or the said plot challenging the aforesaid acquisitions which was contested by the Chittagong Municipality. The said suit was dismissed but some adverse observations were made in the judgment about the title and possession of the Chittagong Municipality and as such it filed First Appeal No. 75 of 1969 in the High Court which was disposed by the High Court Division by a judgment dated 30-1-1981 upholding the decree of the dismissal of the suit finding the title and possession of the municipality in the land of that suit on the basis of the self same orders of acquisition. Against the said judgment the plaintiffs of that suit moved the Appellant Division with a petition for Special Leave to Appeal No. 406 of 1981 whereon leave was granted and the Civil Appeal arising out of it is pending. The defendant No.1 has formulated a scheme for development and establishment of a residential area known as Muradpur Housing Estate covering the said land and other adjoining lands to meet the growing demand of the members of the public and the said scheme has been duly approved by its Works Sub-Committee in its general meeting held on 30-11-81. Thereafter the scheme was referred to the then Controlling Authority namely, the Commissioner, Chittagong Division for necessary action. The said scheme was duly approved by the Government of Bangladesh. The development plan provides for construction of residential and commercial buildings and for establishment of clinic-cum-residence for medical specialists and accordingly public advertisement was made inviting applications from the intending allottees and after allotment the lease deeds have been executed and registered with the allottees. The development works have been validly undertaken and if any injunction is issued the development works and public will suffer. Various development works like drain, road, etc. have been completed long ago. 

 5. Subsequently the defendant No. 1 filed a copy of the judgment of the Appellate Division showing that the said Civil Appeal has been dismissed in the meantime. On an application filed by the plaintiffs the lessees of the defendant No. 1 in the said plots were added as defendants and the added defendant No. 7 also filed a written objection. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge after hearing rejected the application for temporary injunction by a judgment and order dated 17-1-85. 

 Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order the plaintiffs preferred the present appeal. 

 6. Mr Mozammel Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submits that the plaintiffs-appellants have proved a prima facie and arguable case for injunction and also prima facie title to the suit land and, as such, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge erred in not granting injunction. He further submits that unless the injunction is granted, the plaintiffs will suffer irreparable loss and if the defendants in the meantime make constructions the plaintiffs would be put to inconvenience in taking possession in execution of the decree, if any, passed; on the other hand, if the defendants are restrained, they will have to suspend their work for some time and if the suit is dismissed they will get opportunity to make construction and recover compensation from the plaintiffs for the loss they would suffer due to injunction delaying construction and they will not suffer irreparable loss. He further submits that unless the injunction is issued, the lateral support of their eastern hill will slide down due to cutting of hill slopes and as a result, their building situated thereon will collapse and the nature and character of the suit land will be changed creating complication. He further submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge failed to consider the case of the plaintiffs properly and erred in rejecting the application. 

 7. Mr Maqbul Ahmed, the learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant respondent No. 1 submits that the plaintiffs have no prima facie title rather the defendant No. 1 has prima facie title to the suit land inasmuch after the admitted acquisition during the World War, there was no de-requisition nor delivery of possession in favour of the vendors of the plaintiffs. Admittedly the plaintiffs are out of possession of the Suitland and so the plaintiffs by their alleged lease from the ex-Mutawalli acquired no title. He further submits that the court has no jurisdiction to grant any injunction in view of the embargo put by the Martial Law Order No. 40 of 1982 and, as such, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge was justified in rejecting the application. In this connection he further submits that the Chittagong Municipal Corporation is a Corporation as contemplated in Martial Law Order No. 40 of 1982 and the work against which the injunction is sought for is a development work undertaken by the Municipal Corporation and, as such, no injunction can be granted. 

 13. Mr Mozammel Hossain, the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-appellants lastly submits that the Municipal Corporation has nothing to do in the matter but the allottees would make the construction in their respective allotted plots and the bar put by the said Martial law Order has no application in restraining the allottees-defendants and they may be restrained. It appears from the connected papers, bye-laws and the deed of lease filed by the defendant respondent No. 1 that although the allot tees are to construct buildings in their respective allotted plots within 3 years the Corporation has undertaken the overall responsibility for the development of the plan by constructing, roads, parks, drain, etc and it is alleged in the written objection that they have already completed the work of drain and roads long ago and construction to be made by the allottees are part of the development work. So, if the injunction is issued, it will have the effect of injunction with the measure designed to implement the development plan for establishment of Muradpur Housing Estate undertaken by the Chittagong Municipal Corporation with prior approval of the Government and as such the prayer for temporary injunction is barred by Martial Law Order No. 40 of 1982. 

 14. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge did not decide the point touching Martial Law Order No. 40 of 1982. He however, rejected the application for temporary injunction on merit with the findings that the plaintiffs failed to make out a prima facie case and that the balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in favour of the plaintiffs. Admittedly the plaintiffs are out of possession of the suit land and it is in possession of the defendants and the plaintiffs have filed the suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession. There will be no impediment in the way of getting a decree if the plaintiffs are found entitled to, if no temporary injunction is issued and if any construction is made by the defendants during pendency of the suit it will be at their own risk and will not create any bar in executing the decree, if any, passed. So there is no scope for any temporary injunction in the present suit. Hence the plaintiff's prayer for temporary injunction fails on merit also. We, therefore, do not find any error to have been committed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in rejecting the application.
